Story & Plot

A man inherits a palace in rural Mangalpur and plans to host his sister's wedding on the property. However, strange supernatural events and panicked locals soon force him to investigate the building's mysterious past. Directed by Priyadarshan, the horror-comedy blends elements of fantasy, mythology, horror, and romance over its nearly two-and-a-half-hour runtime.

Comedy & Entertainment

The film delivers a healthy dose of humour, horror, and nostalgia, sticking to good old-fashioned storytelling rather than chasing modern trends. Reviewers note that it is genuinely entertaining in parts, offering a fun theatrical experience with a messy, loud, and classic Bollywood horror-comedy style. The blend of humor and intense scenes provides a complete paisa vasool entertainer.

Performances & Direction

The film features a legendary cast led by Akshay Kumar, who delivers a power-packed and memorable role with a blend of humour and intense scenes without a single exaggerated dialogue. The evergreen actress Tabu also gives an impeccable performance. They are joined by supporting cast members including Paresh Rawal, Rajpal Yadav, Wamiqa Gabbi, Jisshu Sengupta, Mithila Palkar, and Asrani.

Strengths

  • Powerful lead performance by Akshay Kumar
  • Impeccable acting from Tabu
  • Hilarious and engaging first half
  • Nostalgic classic Bollywood horror-comedy style
  • Solid theatrical entertainment value

Weaknesses

Despite an interesting concept and a hilarious first half, the movie suffers from uneven execution and a choppy mix of genres. Reviewers note that it offers samplers of mythology, horror, comedy, and romance that whet the appetite but do not fully satisfy, meaning it entertains in parts rather than standing out completely.

Final verdict

Bhooth Bangla delivers a nostalgic and entertaining ride with a strong first half and solid performances from Akshay Kumar and Tabu, though its uneven execution holds it back from greatness. Saiyaara follows two artistic souls, Vaani Batra and Krish Kapoor, as they find harmony and create music together despite their contrasting worlds. Vaani is a closet poet who is devastated when her partner dumps her before their wedding, leading her to stop writing until she bumps into Krish six months later while working as a journalist. As feelings deepen, age and circumstances challenge their undeniable bond in this Bollywood love story directed by Mohit Suri.

Comedy & Entertainment

As a quintessential Bollywood love story focused on a passionate and emotional romance, the film leans into intense romantic storylines and dramatic elements rather than traditional humor. Its entertainment value derives from its visually lush, emotive, and melody-driven experience of old-school romance meeting modern love. The central premise relies on the emotional dynamic between a broken man and the woman he connects with through music.

Performances & Direction

Impressive debutants Ahaan Panday and Aneet Padda power this heartfelt romantic musical with their conviction and chemistry. Ahaan Panday portrays Krish Kapoor, a talented yet emotionally volatile singer, while Aneet Padda plays Vaani Batra, carrying the narrative with their compelling presence alongside supporting cast members Alam Khan, Rajesh Kumar, and Geeta Agrawal Sharma.
